requirements.evidence: Default map and range fallback in Queue::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP/defaultPrefixFor (app/Models/Queue.php:79,151-162); prefixForPriority uses the custom map first (Queue.php:164-173); saving hook normalizes []->null and validates canonical keys, single A-Z values and effective-prefix uniqueness including uncovered 0/10/20 levels (Queue.php:92-149); priority_prefix_map is not added to #[Fillable]. Migration adds issue_date nullable, backfills DATE(issued_at), makes it NOT NULL, swaps the unique index and has a down() (2026_10_29_032258_...:11-31). IssueTicket reads the clock once and reuses $now for the code, issued_at and issue_date (IssueTicket.php:22-34). nextCode filters by queue + issue_date and prefix, skipping malformed and legacy A codes (Ticket.php:253-268). UpdateQueue gains ?array $priorityPrefixMap and turns InvalidArgumentException into ValidationException on 'priority_prefix_map' (UpdateQueue.php:46-58). Factory derives issue_date from issued_at and allocates by priority and that day (TicketFactory.php:318-353). Gaps: the factory always overwrites issue_date, even when the caller passes one explicitly (TicketFactory.php:333). UpdateQueue assigns the map onto the in-memory $queue before the name/slug checks, so a later validation failure leaves the passed instance dirty. None of this is verified by tests.

conventions.evidence: Positive: domain write goes through UpdateQueue with the existing Gate authorization (UpdateQueue.php:48), the map is kept out of #[Fillable] (Queue.php:73), migrations have down(), and docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated (lines 9, 443, 455-472). Deviation: the TDD rule 'No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test' is not met. Only existing assertions were renamed A->N (tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php), and no test covers the new behaviour. Both migration files lack a trailing newline ('\ No newline at end of file'), unlike sibling files.

security.evidence: priority_prefix_map is not mass-assignable (Queue.php:73 unchanged Fillable). UpdateQueue authorizes before touching the map (UpdateQueue.php:48-58). Model-level validation runs on every save (Queue.php:94-96), and the regex value check '/^[A-Z]$/' plus preg_quote in nextCode (Ticket.php:262) keep prefixes safe. No UI or Livewire surface was added. No weaknesses found.

tests.evidence: The only test changes replace 'A001'->'N001' etc. in tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php:483-553. There are no tests for P/E prefixes, independent per-prefix sequences, the daily restart, the legacy A001 -> N001 case, custom maps, map validation (bad keys '-1'/'010'/'foo', 'xx' values, duplicate/merged prefixes, [] -> null), UpdateQueue priorityPrefixMap (set, clear, ValidationException, unchanged queue, authorization), the factory's issue_date alignment or the issued_at=2026-09-28 case, or the migration. Existing tests were not weakened.

simplicity.evidence: Ticket::nextCode accepts its prefix and date in either order with mixed types, regex-sniffing date strings (Ticket.php:218-251). This is speculative flexibility, since every caller passes (queueId, prefix, date). Date parsing swallows errors with catch(\Throwable) and falls back to the raw string (Ticket.php:246-250). The factory has defensive parsing plus an unreachable `if ($issuedAt === null)` (TicketFactory.php:320-330). It also issues an extra Queue::query()->find() per ticket instead of using the loaded relation (TicketFactory.php:350-351). In normalizePriorityPrefixMap, `strlen($value) !== 1` is redundant next to the regex (Queue.php:131).

readability.evidence: Queue.php helpers are clear and documented. nextCode is harder to follow because of the dual-order argument juggling and duplicated branches (Ticket.php:224-237). The useful PHPDoc explaining why codes are ordered by id rather than by string (A999 -> A1000) was removed (Ticket.php:209-213 old). The factory contains dead code (TicketFactory.php:328-330).

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. The MUTABLE_AFTER_CREATE constant was moved above nextCode with no functional change (Ticket.php:195-204 vs. removed 271-281), which is unrelated churn.

issues.explanation: No new tests cover the prefix map, its validation, the daily per-prefix restart, the UpdateQueue parameter or the factory issue_date behaviour, which violates the project's mandatory TDD rule.
nextCode accepts its prefix and date in either order and sniffs dates with a regex, then silently falls back to the raw string when parsing fails, which is unneeded and error-masking complexity.
The map is assigned to the passed Queue instance before the later name/slug validation, so a subsequent ValidationException leaves the caller's model dirty with the new map.
issue_date is always overwritten from issued_at, so an explicitly passed issue_date is silently ignored. The task only asks for issued_at as the default.
The factory has defensive parsing with an unreachable null check and re-queries the Queue for every ticket instead of using the available relation.
The explanatory PHPDoc on insertion-order and malformed-code handling was removed and replaced by a vaguer comment.
The MUTABLE_AFTER_CREATE constant was moved without any functional reason.
Both new migrations lack a trailing newline.

review.summary: The change implements priority-derived prefixes with a validated, non-fillable per-queue map, daily per-prefix sequencing via a new issue_date column with a proper migration, single-clock issuance, UpdateQueue support and doc updates, and the logic looks largely correct. However, it ships no tests for any of the new behaviour (only A->N renames), which breaks the project's mandatory TDD convention, and nextCode and the factory carry needless defensive complexity, so it needs changes before merging.
